name: Louisiana
overview: Louisiana provides a homestead exemption, an income-tested assessment freeze, and a narrow statutory tax credit for people who own their residence but lease its land.

programs.name: Homestead Exemption
programs.maximumBenefit: $7,500 of assessed value, with tax and property limitations.
programs.formulaSummary: Exempt the eligible assessed-value portion from covered ad valorem taxes.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Bona fide owner-occupied homestead; municipal and other constitutional limitations apply.

programs.name: Special Assessment Level
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or specified military, disability or surviving-family categories.
programs.incomeDefinition: Prior-year federal AGI under the constitutional rules.
programs.incomeLimits: Statutory income ceiling applies; use the tax-year-specific application threshold.
programs.maximumBenefit: Future eligible assessed-value increases are limited; the amount depends on the frozen assessment and tax rates.
programs.formulaSummary: Freeze qualifying assessed value at the first eligible year while conditions continue.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Property must qualify for the homestead exemption.
An assessment freeze does not freeze tax rates or necessarily the total bill.

programs.name: Residential Lessees’ Property Tax Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Covered tax on $7,500 assessed value or actual covered tax, whichever is less.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit ad valorem tax on a qualifying residence owned by the occupant where the underlying land is leased.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Residential lessee means a person who owns and occupies the residence, including a mobile home, but does not own its land.
Ordinary apartment renters are not eligible through this provision.
interactions: Available only where the claimant is not otherwise entitled to the homestead exemption.

researchNotes: The narrow lessee credit must not be advertised as a general renter credit.
Housing filters classify ownership of the dwelling: a dwelling owner who rents the underlying land appears under homeowners.
Current constitutional pages contain future-effective amendments; a 2025 comparison must use provisions in force for 2025.
